transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Elaine Wu (CTO, Pacific Biologics), Samir Patel (Head of Infra), Rosa Martinez (Security Lead), Tom Becker (ML Engineer)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Redwood reps walked through on-prem / air-gapped deployment options and constraints. Customer is highly regulated, requires air-gapped deployment with HSM/KMS integration, offline update process, strict audit logs, and hardware procurement constraints (mix of older GPUs / limited racks). Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private, latency/cost expectations, and next steps to run a technical POC and share security artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out time. I'm Lena, I'm the account executive, with Marco Ruiz our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Dr. Elaine Wu: Good thanks, yeah, thanks for making time. We are trying to move through a few vendor checks for the on-prem story.
[00:10] Marco Ruiz: Awesome. Quick run of agenda - confirm requirements, talk constraints for air-gapped environment, update/patch cadence, perf and hardware, and then next steps / POC plan.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Rosa will lead the compliance questions. Tom has some ML sizing notes.
[00:22] Rosa Martinez: Yep. We'll probably interrupt with a bunch of policy questions, fair warning.
[00:26] Tom Becker: Hi all.

[00:30] Lena Park: Great. To start, Elaine, can you give us a quick overview of the use case and success criteria?
[00:36] Dr. Elaine Wu: Sure. We're building internally-facing summarization and QA tools for clinical trial notes and research documents. PII and PHI are involved so we can't send data off premises. The goal is sub-200ms token latencies for interactive UI and throughput of ~2000 tokens per second for overnight batch jobs. Success is meeting compliance and passing our security review plus stable perf in production.
[00:57] Marco Ruiz: OK, thanks. And currently what's your infra? Do you run Kubernetes on prem, or bare-metal? GPU types?
[01:04] Samir Patel: We're a mix. We have a small-ish on-prem cluster; mostly NVIDIA A40s and a couple of V100s in older racks. Storage is on dedicated SAN, and we are not internet-connected in that datacenter - it's air-gapped. Updates happen via signed installer bundles that we ingest via USB or secure transfer agents.
[01:25] Marco Ruiz: Got it. So air-gapped, hardware variety, signed bundles. That aligns with other regulated customers. Quick question - are you open to a hybrid control plane (Redwood control plane hosted, with private data plane in your VPC) or must everything be offline including control plane?
[01:38] Rosa Martinez: Must be fully air-gapped. No external control plane. We maintain an internal control plane for management. Any external telemetry needs explicit approval; by default disabled.
[01:46] Lena Park: Understood. We do offer a fully private package for air-gapped environments - Redwood Private on-prem - that can run with a customer-managed control plane. Marco, do you want to elaborate on how updates work?
[01:56] Marco Ruiz: Sure. For fully air-gapped deployments we provide an offline installer bundle that contains the runtime, model binaries, and signed artifacts. Customers import the bundle via secure media. For patches and model updates we support incremental deltas and signed manifests so you don't have to transfer full images each time. The bundle is compatible with both Kubernetes and bare-metal. There is an OEM-like package and an operator for K8s if you want orchestration.
[02:20] Tom Becker: How big are model binaries? If we're using Llama-3 70B or similar, are you expecting us to host full or quantized variants? We're constrained on memory and some of our nodes are 32GB.
[02:29] Marco Ruiz: Good point. For larger models we recommend quantized variants - 4-bit or 8-bit depending on perf tolerance - which brings memory way down. We also have shard-aware serving and can run model parallel across multiple cards. But that requires network latency between GPUs to be low. With mixed A40/V100 you'd likely need to standardize or isolate workloads to similar hardware to avoid perf variance.
[02:48] Samir Patel: We can't standardize quickly; procurement lead times are long. Is there a way to pin workloads to specific subsets of the pool?
[02:55] Marco Ruiz: Yes, our runtime supports node affinity and pool tagging - you can pin critical low-latency models to newer A40 racks and send background batch jobs to older nodes. There's also autoscale but in air-gapped setups that's typically manual scale via your infra team.
[03:08] Rosa Martinez: On the security front, we need HSM integration for key storage. We also require audit logs, immutable event store, and SAML/SSO with our IdP. Can your private package integrate with internal KMS or HSMs?
[03:20] Marco Ruiz: Yes. We integrate with customer-managed KMS and HSMs via PKCS#11 or compatible interfaces. Keys never leave your network. Audit logs can be stored locally and shipped to your SIEM. We also support SAML SSO and role-based access controls. Note - the control plane pieces that run on your network handle auth; nothing calls back to our hosted services.
[03:37] Rosa Martinez: Good. What about proofs of the binary signing and supply chain? We need SBOMs and reproducible builds or at least signed artifacts with verifiable hashes.
[03:47] Marco Ruiz: We provide signed manifests for every release, and can produce SBOMs for the components in the bundle. Reproducible builds are in roadmap but we do provide cryptographic signatures and a chain of trust that your security team can validate.
[03:58] Dr. Elaine Wu: For model updates, our compliance team will probably ask that we keep model weights in a locked vault and approve them before they go in. How would that workflow work with your offline updater?
[04:08] Marco Ruiz: The offline updater supports a staging process: you receive the signed model artifact, you validate hashes and signatures in your environment, then approve via local manifest to the operator which installs it. The installer can be configured to require multi-sig from your approvers.
[04:20] Tom Becker: Any support for delta quantization patches? Like push smaller quantized delta instead of full model?
[04:25] Marco Ruiz: We can support delta updates for the runtime and model quantization maps; quantization deltas are possible if you keep the same base checkpoint. We'll need to scope that in the POC.

[04:35] [00:04:35] Lena Park: Let's talk telemetry - we heard you want telemetry off by default. How would you like error reporting and usage metrics handled?
[04:43] Rosa Martinez: Off by default. We may allow local collection and periodic offline export to our analytics team. No PII or PHI leaves the network.
[04:51] Marco Ruiz: We can configure telemetry to write to local endpoints (file, syslog, or local metrics ingestion). The agent can be disabled entirely as well.

[05:00] Samir Patel: Network topology - GPUs across racks, is there a recommended topology? Our A40s are in two racks separated by a ToR switch with 100Gb links but hops add latency.
[05:10] Marco Ruiz: For cross-GPU KV cache sharing and model parallelism we recommend RDMA or at least 100Gb with low hop count. If it's higher latency, prefer sharded serving or use per-node smaller models. Our serving runtime adapts but there's perf penalty.
[05:24] Tom Becker: Speaking of perf, can you run benchmarks in our environment?
[05:28] Lena Park: Yes, that's typically the POC - we bring a small benchmark suite and model variants, run inference with your seq lengths and report latency/throughput. We'll need an initial sizing doc from you.
[05:36] Tom Becker: I'll share batch sizes and seq length distributions - most interactive calls are 32-64 tokens, but some longer docs go to 1024. Batches for overnight are large 512-2048 tokens.

[05:48] [00:05:48] Marco Ruiz: Noted. For planning, can you confirm expected concurrent interactive sessions?
[05:52] Dr. Elaine Wu: Target ~50 concurrent interactive users during peak.
[05:56] Marco Ruiz: OK that helps.

[06:00] Rosa Martinez: One more compliance: retention and deletion. Logs and model artifacts - we need FIFO deletion policies and tamper-evident logs.
[06:07] Marco Ruiz: Our private package supports configurable retention policies and we can ingest logs into an append-only store; we also support signed audit logs for tamper evidence.

[06:16] Samir Patel: Any limitations on GPU drivers or kernel modules? Our environment has an older CentOS image.
[06:21] Marco Ruiz: We publish runtime compatibility matrix. Newer runtimes prefer recent drivers; older kernels may require a compatibility shim. We'll include a pre-check script in the bundle to validate OS/drivers before install.

[06:33] Lena Park: Great. Let's cover pricing and contract shape briefly - there are two options: Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) or Private on-prem license plus support. Elaine, do you have a procurement timeline?
[06:44] Dr. Elaine Wu: We're aiming to complete vendor security and run a POC in the next 3-4 weeks, then procure for pilot by end of Q2. Pricing will be evaluated against TCO including hardware upgrades.
[06:56] Lena Park: OK we'll prepare a Dedicated vs Private TCO and model-sizing spreadsheet.

[07:00] Tom Becker: One operational question - model rollback. If a model update causes degradation, can we quickly revert?
[07:06] Marco Ruiz: Yes - installer supports staged rollouts and easy rollback to previous signed manifest. In air-gapped setups you'll still do the manifest approve locally.

[07:15] Rosa Martinez: What's your incident response SLA for on-prem customers? We need clear escalation, forensic support, and patch windows.
[07:24] Lena Park: For enterprise Private customers we include a support SLA and options for accelerated patching. We'll include the SLA options in the security pack.

[07:31] [00:07:31] Marco Ruiz: Quick note - some of our customers in med/finance set up an internal model registry with approvals, plus a canary path that runs only on a subset of nodes. That could be a good model for you.
[07:44] Dr. Elaine Wu: That aligns with our process.

[07:48] Lena Park: Alright let's recap and confirm next steps.
[07:52] Marco Ruiz: Action items: we'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, SBOM process) and an architecture diagram for the offline updater. We'll also prepare a TCO spreadsheet comparing Dedicated vs Private and initial model sizing notes. We propose a POC week w/c 2026-03-23 if that works for you.
[08:10] Dr. Elaine Wu: Works for us tentatively. We'll also send you procurement constraints and a list of compliance artifacts we need.

[08:18] Rosa Martinez: We'll provide a whitelist for the installer and our compliance checklist.

[08:22] Lena Park: Perfect. Any final questions?
[08:24] Tom Becker: Not from me. Thanks, helpful call.
[08:27] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone.
[08:29] Lena Park: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the deck.

[08:33] End of call.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache, "H M S" for HSM), speaker gaps, and truncated sentences present.
